title: French Defense: Advance, Steinitz | The Sensei Speedrun | GM Naroditsky

moves.spoken: The French again, and against it the plan is the Steinitz: the pawn to e5 for the Advance, but instead of the usual c3 to prop up d4, a very odd-looking treatment is coming.
moves.teaches: The Steinitz Advance skips c3 — White leans on the e5-clamp rather than the d4-pawn.

moves.spoken: Black hits with the pawn to c5 and now the signature move — the knight to f3, leaving d4 to its fate. It looks strange and it scores heavily: development and the e5-clamp matter more than the pawn.
moves.teaches: Nf3 over c3: trade the d4-pawn's defence for speed and the cramping e5-pawn.

moves.spoken: Bishop to d3, and the capture on d4 simply doesn't matter. The whole idea is to keep developing and let the e5-pawn do the cramping while Black spends moves on a pawn that was never the point.
moves.teaches: Meet ...cxd4 with calm development — the initiative outweighs the pawn.
moves.plans: Bd3, then resolve the centre favourably.

moves.spoken: Rather than castle, capture on c5. This reaches exactly the pawn structure Black would have got by taking on d4 — except here White never sacrificed the pawn, and the position is already unpleasant for Black.
moves.teaches: dxc5 can reach the same structure as a pawn sac without paying the pawn — take the free version.
moves.plans: dxc5, recapture, keep the extra tempo.

moves.spoken: The knight to c3 is the principled, most testing move. Two things frame the position: Black has no dark-squared bishop, so his remaining bishop is the bad one, and the Greek-gift sacrifice on h7 is quietly on the cards the moment Black castles kingside.
moves.teaches: Note the missing dark-squared bishop and a lurking Bxh7+ before choosing where to develop.
moves.plans: Nc3, eye the light squares and the h7 sac.

moves.spoken: With the queen on c7, look at where the knight can go. The knight to b5 is thematic — it wants to sink its teeth into d6, the hole in Black's camp.
moves.teaches: Reroute the knight toward a hole the opponent can't cover — here, d6.
moves.plans: Nb5, aiming at the d6 outpost.

moves.spoken: The knight to d6 with check, and it's not too late to strike — d6 is uncovered, so the knight jumps in without preparation. After the trade, a monster pawn lands on d6 and Black's position already stinks.
moves.teaches: When the outpost is uncovered, occupy it with tempo before the opponent can defend it.
moves.plans: Nd6+, then a cramping pawn on d6.

moves.spoken: First eliminate the knight with the capture on g6 — because bishop to f4 straight away would just hang the bishop. Take, then play bishop f4: it supports the d6-pawn, and with no dark-squared bishop, Black has nothing to challenge it with.
moves.teaches: Remove the defender/attacker first, then occupy the square the recapture no longer contests.

moves.spoken: Notice the extra point: recapturing wrecks Black's kingside pawns and opens the h-file, and if Black castles short he steps into an attack down it — while, other than the rook on h8, Black has no kingside firepower to make that file cut both ways.
moves.teaches: Opening a file against a king only helps the side with pieces to pour down it.
moves.plans: Damage the kingside, aim rooks at the h-file.

moves.spoken: The knight to g5 is prophylaxis and attack in one. Its main job is to stop ...f6 — because then e6 would hang — and at the same time it joins the hunt on Black's king.
moves.teaches: A single knight move can both prevent the opponent's freeing break and attack the king.

moves.spoken: Time for the rook lift — the rook to e3, ready to swing to h3 and join the queen against the king. The pieces are all pointing the same way; now they converge.
moves.teaches: Lift a rook along the third rank to add a heavy piece to the kingside attack.
moves.plans: Re3-h3, then bring the queen in.

moves.spoken: With the rook lifted, the queen comes to g4 and the threats mount — rook to h3 next, and the mating net tightens. Everything is in place; the attack plays itself.
moves.teaches: Once the pieces are massed, add the queen last and the mate threats appear on their own.
